transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um... I guess the main reason I'm here is just... having some trouble at work. 

Lately, anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work... it's just difficult. Like doing the monthly reports, or having to plan out a multi-site health event. It feels like I just hit a wall. I keep putting it off, even when I know it matters. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Has this difficulty with focusing and starting tasks been a struggle for you for most of your life, or is this a relatively new issue?

No, not my whole life. It's... newer. I guess it's been about a year and eleven months, give or take. 

Um... a friend of mine died back then. And I ended up taking on more of the league and outreach responsibilities. So... yeah. Just since then, really.
Beyond the trouble with focusing at work, have you been feeling sad, down, or have you lost interest in the things you usually enjoy?

Um... no. Not really. 

I don't think I've been feeling sad, or... anything like that. I still do the things I normally enjoy. It's really just... the work stuff.
Beyond the difficulty with your work tasks, have you been feeling particularly nervous, worried, or on edge?
No, not really. I mean... I wouldn't say I'm nervous. Just... frustrated with the work stuff, I guess. But no, not worried or on edge.
Have you found yourself acting out or behaving in ways that you normally wouldn't, such as being more aggressive, reckless, or having more conflicts with people around you since this started?
No. Nothing like that. I haven't been aggressive or... acting out. I don't really get into conflicts with people.
Have you noticed any physical changes, such as a racing heart, muscle tension, or stomach issues, when you are trying to work on these tasks?
No... I don't think so. Physically, I feel fine. I haven't noticed any... stomach issues or a racing heart. Just normal, I guess.
Since the time your friend passed away, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite?
No... sleep's been okay, I think. And my appetite hasn't changed. Just... normal.
When you are at work and feel like you've hit that wall with your tasks, do you find yourself feeling irritable or annoyed with your colleagues or the work environment?
No, not really... I don't get annoyed with them. It's not their fault. I just... keep to myself when that happens, mostly.
When you feel like you've hit that wall with your work, do you find yourself withdrawing from your coworkers or spending more time alone than you did before your friend passed away?
I don't think so. I mean, I've always kind of kept to myself at work anyway. I haven't really noticed a difference.

Since your friend passed away, have you found yourself intentionally breaking rules, skipping work, or failing to meet your professional obligations in a way that goes beyond just having difficulty focusing?
No, no. Nothing like that. I just... I go to work and try to get things done. I haven't been skipping or breaking rules. Just struggling to concentrate, that's all.
Have you noticed any change in how you treat your responsibilities or how you interact with others, such as being more rebellious or defiant, since your friend passed away?
No. I haven't been... defiant. I just do my job. Like I said, I just have a hard time focusing. That's it.
Does this difficulty with your work tasks cause you significant distress, or does it interfere with your ability to function in other areas of your life outside of work?

Well... I'm still getting by, I guess. At work and, you know, outside of it. But... yeah, it's frustrating. People have had to cover some gaps for me lately. I've let a few deadlines slip. It's... embarrassing, honestly. Having to make last-minute apologies to coworkers. And friends, too. I just... I don't like it.
When you think about the fact that you've let deadlines slip and have had to apologize to others, do you feel an overwhelming sense of hopelessness or despair about your situation?
No, I wouldn't say hopeless. I mean, it bothers me, but... I don't feel despair or anything. Just... annoyed with myself, I guess.
When you are struggling with these work tasks, do you ever feel a sense of restlessness or find it hard to sit still?
No... not really. I can sit at my desk just fine. It's just... hard to actually get the work done. But I don't feel restless or anything.
When you have to face these work tasks that you are struggling with, do you experience any internal feelings of apprehension or a sense of dread?
No... not dread. I wouldn't say that. It's just work. I just... have trouble finishing it sometimes, like I said. But I don't feel apprehensive about it.
When you think about the fact that you have been struggling to finish your work, do you find that you are frequently tearful or cry more easily than you used to?
No. I don't... cry. Not at all. It's just frustration, that's all.

When you think about the frustration you feel regarding these missed deadlines, does that frustration manifest primarily as a lingering sense of being 'down' or 'blue', or is it more of a sense of being 'on edge' or 'jittery'?
Neither, really. I don't... I wouldn't say I feel down. Or jittery. It's just... annoying. Just annoyed at myself for not getting it done, I guess. That's it.
When you have to apologize to your coworkers for missing deadlines, do you feel a sense of guilt or remorse for how your performance is affecting them?
No. Not really. I just... apologize and we move on. I don't really dwell on it past that. It's just work.
Have these missed deadlines or your difficulty with work tasks caused any negative consequences, such as reprimands from your supervisor or a negative impact on your job security?

I mean... I'm still getting by. Nobody's fired me or anything. But... yeah, things slip. People have had to cover for me when I drop the ball. It's... embarrassing, having to make those last-minute apologies to my coworkers. Or even to friends outside of work. But I'm still managing, mostly.
When you have to apologize to your coworkers or friends for missing those deadlines, do you feel a sense of embarrassment or shame that lingers throughout the day?
No, not really. It doesn't linger. I just... I say sorry and that's it. I don't really think about it after that.
